source_request: 시각 의미 데이터와 후보팩에 반영해줘. 시각 의미 데이터의 대체 표현을 추가/보강하는 작업을 중심으로 진행하고 후보팩에도 잘 반영해줘. 그 다음 독립된 서브에이전트 3개에서 각각 서로 다른 컨셉으로 반영한 키워드가 이미지에 실제로 반영되는지까지 테스트할 수 있는 랜덤한 복잡한 컨셉을 정하여 테스트케이스를 마련하고 첨부한 이미지를 활용하여 프롬프트 작성하고 이미지 생성하도록 하여 잘 반영되었는지 테스트해줘.
interpreted_intent: The requester asks for random, complex visual qualification concepts and reference-guided image generation. Randomly selected coordinator-owned labels supply the test stimuli, not requester definitions. I choose a contemporary staged dress rehearsal in which a single fictional adult performer joins an embroidered tortoise-and-entwined-snake chest emblem with a head nimbus and whole-body mandorla. This costume-and-light installation makes stitched and luminous framing relate to the same owner. A separate museum display was considered but rejected because it weakens that relation. Quiet attraction is a subtle supporting presence at saved sensual=1, through camera awareness, face light, and fabric bearing; fetish=0 adds no focus, surreal=0 keeps the light forms physically staged, creativity=1 permits restrained design choices. The image is a fictional contemporary artwork, with no claim of an actual historical ceremony or sect.
subject: A reference-guided fictional adult performer, age 28, wearing a midnight-blue ceremonial-style silk robe whose flat chest panel carries 의례복 자수의 거북과 감긴 뱀: one tortoise and one snake entwined around that same shell as metallic-thread embroidery.
setting: A contemporary black-box theater installation with 두광과 전신 만돌라: one circular head nimbus behind the performer and a separate complete pointed-almond full-body mandorla behind that same performer, on a dry low platform with receding charcoal scrims.
event: During a staged photographic performance, the performer gently holds the robe side seams at hip height to display the single tortoise-and-coiled-snake emblem as the head nimbus and whole-body mandorla align behind her.
visual_priorities: The reference-guided adult face and dark bob hold a quiet camera-facing presence.
One joined embroidered tortoise-and-snake emblem remains exposed on the performer’s flat chest panel, including a readable coil around the shell.
The small head nimbus and the larger complete pointed-almond mandorla enclose the same performer at distinctly different scales.
Tangible silk folds, stitched metal threads, and engineered light shapes connect the costume to a contemporary stage.
baseline_prompt_en: An editorial photograph for a complex visual test concept features a reference-guided fictional adult performer, age 28, during a staged photographic performance in a contemporary black-box theater. The attached portrait guides visible eye, face, and bob-hair appearance only. Her large dark brown eyes, soft oval face, and chin-length dark bob with wispy fringe carry a quietly magnetic presence. She stands facing the camera on a low dry black platform, both shoes planted, holding the side seams of her wide-sleeved midnight-blue silk robe at hip height with gently bent elbows so its central chest panel lies flat. On that panel, large metallic embroidery depicts one tortoise with a domed segmented shell, a clear head, four legs, and a short tail; one slender snake with a distinct head forms a continuous coil around that same shell, crossing over its near edge. The stitched animals belong to one joined emblem on the worn robe, their gold and silver threads catching the grazing light. Directly behind her head, one warm-gold circular luminous disk forms a head nimbus. Behind the same performer, a separate tall cool-white mandorla has two bowed luminous sides meeting in sharp almond-shaped cusps above her hair and below both shoes, visibly enclosing her entire body. The small head circle and large pointed-almond light outline are simultaneously complete and distinct. Their grounded stage construction reads as a contemporary costume-and-light artwork. Her hands draw the fabric just outward, leaving the emblem exposed. A soft sidelight warms her face and the sculptural robe folds; shallow amber shadows separate the body from the cooler light forms. Two open charcoal scrim panels recede into the wings. Use a frontal full-figure composition with breathing room around both pointed tips and enough resolved detail to read the shell, snake coil, and stitched texture. Eyes lead, then the chest emblem, then the two nested light scopes. The intended image feels intimate and poised at the moment a costume fitting becomes a still performance.
